subject: Science
title: Light: Reflection and Refraction
summary: How light reflects from plane and spherical mirrors and refracts through a glass slab and spherical lenses: the laws, the six ray diagrams for a concave mirror, the New Cartesian sign convention, the mirror and lens formulas, magnification, refractive index and the power of a lens. It is the most numerical-heavy chapter of Class 10 physics and a ray diagram or a mirror/lens-formula problem from it appears in the board paper every year.

exam_profile.weightage: Class 10 Science is one 80-mark board paper. This chapter belongs to the unit Natural Phenomena together with Chapter 10 (The Human Eye and the Colourful World); the unit carries about 12 marks. From this chapter alone you can typically expect 6 to 8 marks: one or two 1-mark items, a 2- or 3-mark numerical or ray diagram, and a share of a 5-mark question or a case-based passage on mirrors or lenses.

question_types.note: Where to place the object for a given kind of image, which mirror or lens from a description (rear-view, dentist, dictionary), sign of focal length, meaning of a magnification value, speed of light from a refractive index, what happens when half a lens is covered.

Convex mirror as rear-view mirror; light bending towards the normal in a denser medium; absolute refractive index never less than 1; a lens of negative power being concave; emergent ray from a glass slab being parallel to the incident ray.

Define principal focus or focal length with a diagram; one small mirror-formula or lens-formula numerical; compare optical densities from refractive indices; define power of a lens and find focal length from power; ray diagram for a single incident ray on a convex mirror.

Laws of refraction plus a definition of absolute refractive index; a numerical on a concave mirror or convex lens with nature of the image; two ray diagrams for a convex mirror; a numerical on the speed of light in two media; the meaning of a given magnification with the mirror named.

Ray diagrams for a concave mirror or convex lens for two or three object positions with uses; laws of refraction and refractive index with a numerical on speed of light; definition of power and combination of lenses with a lens-formula numerical; one combined question on mirrors and lenses with an OR choice.

A passage on a solar furnace or a rear-view mirror, or an observation table of object and image distances for a convex lens from which you find the focal length and the position giving a same-sized image.

hot_topics: Ray diagrams for a concave mirror (all six object positions) and the two convex mirror diagrams
Mirror formula and lens formula numericals with the New Cartesian sign convention
Magnification: sign, meaning of a given value, and m = −v/u for mirrors versus m = v/u for lenses
Refractive index: definition, n = c/v, relative refractive index, speed of light in a medium
